newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - October expiry sparks spike in FTSE 100.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - October expiry sparks spike in FTSE 100.

text.p: The FTSE 100 spiked higher in late morning trading on Friday, propelled by the expiration of October index options, traders said.
The 0930 GMT expiration bolstered trading volume in index options, as positions from the expiring October contract were closed out or rolled over into other contract months.
November FTSE options were mostly sold, while December FTSE options were relatively well bid, traders said.
One trader attributed this disparity to short-term traders taking advantage of options time decay ahead of the weekend. November options decay at a faster rate than December options.
Most of the volume in the American-style FTSE 100 options was in the November 4,200 calls.
Almost 6,200 lots had traded by 1307 GMT.
More than 2,500 lots traded in the November 4050 puts, and between 1,000 and 1,500 lots traded in November 3850 puts, November 4000 calls and November 4050 calls.
Among December options, volume was heaviest in the December 3500 puts. More than 1,000 lots traded in both the December 3850 calls and December 4200 puts.
The underlying blue chip index was up 18.3 points at 4,060.4, just below its record at 4,061.4 set earlier.
In equity options, traders noted a bearish spread established in British Petroleum options, where 500 January 650 puts were sold at 3-1/2p against the purchase of 500 January 600 puts at 13p.
British Petroleum shares were up 2-1/2p to 680p.
Traders also noted the purchase of 500 February 280 Rolls-Royce calls at 8-1/2p. The shares were trading at 261p, up 4-1/2p.
